headline: Congress funds five major spending areas for the rest of fiscal year 2026, briefly funds Homeland Security, and extends many expiring programs.
what_it_does: This law pays for many federal agencies through the end of fiscal year 2026, including Defense, Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, Transportation, Housing, Treasury, the courts, and the State Department. It funds the Department of Homeland Security only through February 13, 2026, mostly at 2025 levels, unless a full Homeland Security funding bill passes sooner. It also extends a long list of programs that were set to expire, such as the National Flood Insurance Program, the TANF cash assistance program for low-income families, trade benefits for Haiti and sub-Saharan Africa, and several health care and immigration programs.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees and contractors at the funded agencies
who_it_affects.how: Their agencies have funding for the rest of the fiscal year, which keeps operations running.
They are funded only through February 13, 2026, mostly at 2025 levels, unless a full-year bill passes first.

who_it_affects.group: Homeowners and renters who buy federal flood insurance
who_it_affects.how: The National Flood Insurance Program is extended so policies can continue to be sold and renewed.

who_it_affects.group: Low-income families who get TANF cash assistance
who_it_affects.how: The TANF program is extended so benefits and state grants can continue.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that trade with Haiti and sub-Saharan African countries
who_it_affects.how: Special trade preferences for goods from these countries are extended.

who_it_affects.group: Military service members and the Defense Department
who_it_affects.how: Defense programs receive full-year funding for fiscal year 2026.
TSA's program that lets outside groups pay for extra screening services is extended.
The U.S. Grain Standards Act, which covers grain inspection and grading, is extended.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted February 3, 2026; most funding runs through the end of fiscal year 2026 (September 30, 2026), while Homeland Security funding runs through February 13, 2026, or until its full-year bill is passed.
